C9000077.statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 077 (Fourier restriction for positively curved surfaces.; papers: Elliptic capacity propagation and Fourier restriction to the sphere; Diagonal Fourier extension for positively curved surfaces in three dimensions; Lean status: UNFORMALIZED (No Lean proof in openai/math)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.

ELLIPTIC_MAIN.statement: For every bounded measurable g on S^2 and every p>3, ||Eg||_Lp(R^3) <= C_p ||g||_Linfinity(S^2).

DIAGONAL_MAIN.statement: For compact smooth positively curved Sigma in R^3, possibly with smooth boundary, and 3<p<infinity, ||E_Sigma f||_Lp(R^3) <= C_(Sigma,p)||f||_Lp(Sigma).

ELLIPTIC_PACKET.statement: pkt:main: A_m(T_m d)^3 <= C m^(10 kappa+eta) G_(delta,1)(d)^3 for all finite complex arrays and permitted coordinate masks.

ELLIPTIC_EXTREMAL_GLOBAL.statement: The capacity decomposition, extremal estimates, and global packet globalization convert the packet bound into the elliptic main theorem.

ELLIPTIC_GEOMETRY.statement: geo:main: elliptic capacity propagates to terminal-bin concentration at every strict exponent below 1+2s-10 kappa.

E_HEREDITY.statement: ent:finite-states, ent:regularization, and ent:tangent-realization supply bounded-ambiguity sheared states and hereditary support and conditional-weight bounds.

E_SCALAR_PROFILE.statement: proj:scalar and proj:parameter-profile supply scalar inequalities and K(Y,R)=sY+theta(R-lambda Y)_+ at the increasing tie.

E_ASPECT.statement: The aspect analysis and local path control combine the scalar and tied inequalities into the propagation exponent.

E_PROJECTION.statement: proj:projection: dense direction-dependent point restrictions with projection support exponent u imply u >= min{k,(k+sigma)/2,1}.

RW_FINITE.statement: Ren--Wang arXiv:2308.08819v2 Theorem 4.1: finite incident tube pencils obey the exponent min{k,(k+sigma)/2,1} in addition to pencil size.

E_RADIAL.statement: proj:radial: a Frostman s0<=1 planar law with power-light strips has power-small pair exceptions to every radial exponent sigma<s0 at fixed power scales.

E_PRODUCT.statement: proj:product: under its time, positive-tilt and affine hereditary hypotheses, pinned products have the stated dense-strip or power-light-strip Frostman conclusions.

E_TIED.statement: proj:tied: at lambda=1 and theta>0, the actual tangent has g,H >= f_s(p), without separate middle-pair rates or independent parameters.

DIAGONAL_PACKET.statement: thm:packet supplies the normalized packet-capacity and cubic coefficient bounds for diagonal extension.

DIAGONAL_SPARSE.statement: prop:discrete and prop:sparse convert packet and translated-tube density estimates into sparse-ball extension bounds.

KAKeya_TRANSLATED.statement: The translated-tube Kakeya maximal theorem cited by the diagonal density argument is an additional external input, not established here.

DIAGONAL_GLOBAL.statement: thm:graph globalizes the sparse-ball bounds to loss-free global extension for elliptic graphs.

DIAGONAL_SURFACE_TRANSFER.statement: Finite elliptic charts, smooth windows, and surface Jacobians transfer thm:graph to compact positively curved surfaces.

CP_QUANTITATIVE.statement: For every realizing sequence of bounded planar laws with time Frostman exponent 0<s<=1, positive tilt exponent, and the stated affine hereditary simultaneous-refinement bounds, the dense-strip and power-light-strip conclusions of proj:product hold uniformly under arbitrary dense incidences. With the stated matched spatial support and weight realizations, the equal-slope rates satisfy g,H>=f_s(p). The nonlinear mechanism has the explicit finite bound recorded in CP_NONLINEAR_CHAIN.

CP_CONDITIONAL_ENTROPY.statement: For probability laws pi,mu, every measurable incidence E of product mass alpha>0, and every finite-valued query-dependent map T_f, put beta(f)=mu(E_f), S={beta>0}, and K_f=(mu x mu){T_f(v)=T_f(v')}. If integral_S K_f dpi<=K, then H(T_F(V)|F;(pi x mu)|E)>=-log K+2 log alpha. The density coefficient 2 is optimal without additional hypotheses.

CP_NONLINEAR_CHAIN.statement: Let delta=1/b for dyadic b>=16, J>=4, n=J-3, 0<a<s<=1, A,B>=1 and delta<=g<=1/4. Let nu on [-1,1]^2 be Frostman s with constant A at radii [delta,1]. Suppose original normalized target cells at levels j=3,...,J-1 have the same bounds outside masses beta_j, and distinct pairs have original reverse radial exponent a with constant B outside mass gamma. For Q_f(d)=(r_d-r_f)(t_d-t_f), every incidence E whose final delta^J output support has at most N bins per pin has product mass rho<=gamma+sum_j beta_j+A(2g)^s+sqrt(8K0) N^(1/(2n))(delta/g)^(a/2), where K0=65536 A(A+B)/(s-a).

CP_RADIAL_BOOTSTRAP.statement: For every 0<a<s<=1, a planar Frostman s law with arbitrarily small losses and uniformly power-small mass in strips of every fixed positive power width has power-small pair exceptions to the original centered radial a bounds on every fixed finite power grid. This follows from the finite Ren--Wang input via a finite dispersed/concentrated-tube bootstrap, not from a Hausdorff-dimension discretization.

CP_WEIGHTED_OVERLAPS.statement: Under the matched equal-slope spatial rate realizations of proj:tied, every dense parameter restriction yields a dense set of full-spatial overlaps of exponent L=p+H+g. Rich inputs have dense weight for one original conditional Frostman (p+g) planar law and scalar projections w_f+(r_d-r_f)(t_d-t_f)x with support exponent at most g. The coefficient theorem and the weighted projection test then imply g>=f_s(p), while monotonicity and the off-tie scalar bound imply H>=f_s(p).
